# Requesting a New KPI (SOP-02)

## Purpose
This procedure explains how anyone at Kestrel can request a new KPI, and how duplicates are avoided.

## Roles
- **Requester:** any employee with a business question that no existing KPI answers.
- **Data steward:** checks for duplicates and assigns an owner.
- **KPI owner:** the domain head who will be accountable for the new KPI.

## Steps
1. The requester raises a "New KPI" request in the data service portal, giving the business question, a proposed definition and the intended audience.
2. The data steward searches the KPI Glossary Summary (POL-04) for an existing KPI with the same meaning. Similar names are checked with care; for example Active Customer (KPI-006) and Active User (KPI-020) measure different things.
3. If a matching KPI exists, the request is closed and the requester is pointed to it.
4. If not, the data steward assigns the KPI owner from the relevant domain and a new id in the form KPI-NNN (see SOP-07).
5. The KPI owner writes the definition using the KPI template. It is published as Provisional with version 0.1.
6. Certification then follows SOP-01.

## Service level
The data steward responds to a new request within 10 working days.

## Related documents
- SOP-01 KPI Certification Process
- SOP-07 Naming Conventions

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Data Governance
Status: Certified
Version: 1.1
Effective date: 2025-02-01
Domain: Governance

Naming Conventions (SOP-07) | part 1
# Naming Conventions (SOP-07)

## Purpose
Consistent names make KPIs, tables and dashboards easy to find and hard to confuse.

## Roles
- **Data steward:** assigns ids and checks names before publishing.

## Rules
1. **KPI ids:** KPI- followed by three digits, for example KPI-014. Ids are never reused.
2. **Deprecated versions:** keep the original id with a version suffix, for example KPI-007-V1.
3. **KPI names:** plain English in Title Case. Use "Rate" or "%" for ratios (for example Return Rate, Gross Margin %). Include the time window in the name when it is part of the definition, for example "Active Customer (30-day)".
4. **Catalog ids:** CAT- followed by two digits, for example CAT-02.
5. **Tables:** lower case snake_case plural nouns, for example `sales_orders`, `nps_responses`.
6. **Dashboards:** Title Case ending in "Dashboard", except the Executive KPI Pack and the Supply Chain Control Tower, which keep their established names.
7. **Documents:** SOP-NN for procedures, POL-NN for policies and standards.
8. **Similar names:** a new KPI name must not differ from an existing one by a single word unless both definitions explain the difference (see KPI-006 and KPI-020).

## Related documents
- SOP-02 Requesting a New KPI

# Dashboard Publishing Standard (SOP-06)

## Purpose
This standard sets the rules every dashboard must meet before it is shared outside its own team.

## Roles
- **Dashboard owner:** builds and maintains the dashboard; listed in the data catalog.
- **Data steward:** checks the dashboard against this standard before publishing.

## Rules
1. Every published dashboard must have an entry in the data catalog with an owner, a refresh schedule and its linked KPIs.
2. Every KPI tile must show the KPI id and version, for example "KPI-007 v2.0".
3. Provisional KPIs must carry a visible "Provisional" label on their tile.
4. Deprecated KPIs must be removed from all dashboards on their deprecation date.
5. The Executive KPI Pack may only contain Certified KPIs. No exceptions.
6. Each dashboard shows the time of the last data refresh.
7. A dashboard can only be Certified if all its tiles use Certified KPIs or carry the Provisional label.

## Steps to publish
1. The dashboard owner requests a review in the data service portal.
2. The data steward checks rules 1 to 7 and records the result.
3. If all rules pass, the dashboard is published and its catalog entry is updated.

## Related documents
- SOP-01 KPI Certification Process
- SOP-03 Metric Change Management
- SOP-05 Data Quality Incidents

# Data Access Requests (SOP-04)

## Purpose
This procedure explains how to get access to a dashboard or a source table. Access depends on the data classification in POL-03.

## Roles
- **Requester:** the employee who needs access.
- **Line manager:** confirms the business need.
- **Data owner:** the owner listed in the data catalog for that asset.
- **Head of Data Governance:** approves access to Restricted data.

## Steps
1. The requester raises an "Access request" in the data service portal, naming the asset from the data catalog and the reason.
2. The line manager approves the business need.
3. For Internal data, access is granted after step 2.
4. For Confidential data (for example the `customers` table), the data owner must also approve.
5. For Restricted data, the Head of Data Governance must also approve, and access is time-limited to 90 days.
6. The platform team grants access within 5 working days of the final approval.

## Reviews
Data owners review the access list for their assets every 6 months and remove anyone who no longer needs it. Leavers lose all access on their last working day.

## Related documents
- POL-03 Data Classification Standard
- POL-01 Data Governance Policy

Gross Margin % (KPI-002) | part 1
# Gross Margin % (KPI-002)

## Definition
Gross Margin % is the share of Net Revenue left after paying for the goods that were sold. It shows how profitable the product mix is before store, logistics and head office costs.

## Formula
Gross Margin % = (Net Revenue - Cost of goods sold) / Net Revenue x 100

Net Revenue follows KPI-001. Cost of goods sold (COGS) is the landed cost of items sold, including freight from suppliers to distribution centres.

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly and year to date.
- Split by product category and channel.
- Concession sales are excluded because Kestrel only earns a commission on them.

## Source tables
- `sales_orders`: net value and landed cost per order line
- `returns`: refunded value and restocked cost

## Dashboards
- Executive KPI Pack

## Caveats and exclusions
- Items that are returned and restocked reverse their COGS.
- Damaged returns that are written off stay in COGS.
- Stock shrinkage (theft, damage in store) is not included here; Finance reports it separately.
- Store labour and delivery to customers are not part of COGS.

## Change history
- v1.3 (2025-09-15): inbound freight added to COGS.
- v1.0 (2024-09-01): first certified version.

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Finance Analytics
Status: Certified
Version: 1.3
Effective date: 2025-09-15
Domain: Finance

Net Revenue (KPI-001) | part 1
# Net Revenue (KPI-001)

## Definition
Net Revenue is the total value of sales across stores, app and web after discounts, returns and refunds, excluding sales tax. It is the base revenue figure used by every other revenue-based KPI at Kestrel.

## Formula
Net Revenue = Gross sales value - Discounts - Returns and refunds - Sales tax

## Grain and filters
- Calculated daily, reported weekly and monthly.
- Split by channel (store, app, web), region and product category.
- Staff purchases are included at the discounted price; test transactions are excluded.

## Source tables
- `sales_orders`: gross value, discount and tax per order
- `returns`: refunded value and refund date

## Dashboards
- Executive KPI Pack
- Sales Performance Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Gift card sales are not revenue when sold; they count when the card is redeemed.
- Returns are deducted in the month the refund is processed, not the month of the original sale. Return Rate (KPI-019) uses the month of sale instead.
- Delivery charges paid by customers are included.

## Change history
- v2.1 (2025-07-01): gift cards moved to recognition at redemption.
- v2.0 (2025-01-01): returns and refunds deducted.
- v1.0 (2024-04-01): first certified version.

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Finance Analytics
Status: Certified
Version: 2.1
Effective date: 2025-07-01
Domain: Finance

Stockout Rate (KPI-017) | part 1
# Stockout Rate (KPI-017)

## Definition
Stockout Rate is the share of products that should be available in a location but have no sellable stock. It shows how often customers find an empty shelf or an out-of-stock product page.

## Formula
Stockout Rate % = Active SKU-location pairs with zero sellable units at the 06:00 snapshot / Total active SKU-location pairs x 100

An active SKU-location pair is a product that is in the current range for that store or for online.

## Grain and filters
- Calculated daily, reported weekly.
- Split by location, region and product category.
- Online availability uses distribution centre stock.

## Source tables
- `inventory_snapshots`: SKU, location, sellable units, range status, snapshot time

## Dashboards
- Supply Chain Control Tower

## Caveats and exclusions
- Discontinued products and seasonal products outside their season are excluded.
- Damaged or reserved units are not sellable and count as zero.
- A product that sells out at noon and is refilled before the next 06:00 snapshot is not counted.

## Change history
- v1.1 (2025-09-01): snapshot time moved from midnight to 06:00.
- v1.0 (2025-02-01): first certified version.

## Ownership and status

Customer Lifetime Value (KPI-011) | part 1
# Customer Lifetime Value (KPI-011)

## Definition
Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) estimates the total gross margin an identified customer will generate for Kestrel over their whole relationship. It is used to decide how much to spend on acquiring and keeping customers.

## Formula
CLV = Average annual gross margin per active customer x Expected customer lifetime in years

Expected lifetime = 1 / Annual churn rate, where the annual churn rate comes from KPI-007 v2. The lifetime is capped at 5 years.

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly.
- Split by loyalty tier and acquisition channel.
- Staff and test accounts are excluded.

## Source tables
- `sales_orders`: margin per order, customer id
- `returns`: refunded value
- `customers`: loyalty tier, acquisition channel

## Dashboards
- Customer 360 Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Provisional: the model is still being validated against actual customer histories.
- Uses gross margin, not revenue. Older team estimates based on revenue are much higher and are not valid.
- Not approved for board reporting or the Executive KPI Pack.

## Change history
- v0.7 (2026-05-15): changed from revenue basis to gross margin basis.
- v0.5 (2026-01-10): first draft.

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Customer Analytics
Status: Provisional
Version: 0.7
Effective date: 2026-05-15
Domain: Customer

Customer Acquisition Cost (KPI-014) | part 1
# Customer Acquisition Cost (KPI-014)

## Definition
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is the average marketing spend needed to win one new identified customer. A new customer is someone whose first ever completed order falls in the period.

## Formula
CAC = Acquisition marketing spend in the period / New customers acquired in the period

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly and quarterly.
- Split by marketing channel (paid search, paid social, affiliates, print).
- Only campaigns tagged as acquisition are included.

## Source tables
- `marketing_spend`: campaign, channel, objective tag, spend, agency fees
- `customers`: customer id, first order date, acquisition channel

## Dashboards
- Marketing Effectiveness Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Brand and retention campaigns are excluded from spend.
- Agency fees are included in spend from v1.1.
- Channel-level CAC uses the acquisition channel recorded on the customer. Customers with no recorded channel only count in the total.
- Compare with Customer Lifetime Value (KPI-011) to judge payback, but note CLV is still Provisional.

## Change history
- v1.1 (2025-12-01): agency fees added to spend.
- v1.0 (2025-03-15): first certified version.

# Net Revenue Retention (KPI-010)

## Definition
Net Revenue Retention (NRR) measures how much net revenue Kestrel keeps from an existing group of customers over 12 months. It includes growth from those customers and losses from customers who stop buying. New customers acquired during the period are excluded.

## Formula
NRR % = (Net revenue in the current 12 months from the base cohort / Net revenue in the prior 12 months from the same cohort) x 100

The base cohort is every identified customer with at least one order in the prior 12-month window. Net revenue follows KPI-001 (after discounts and returns, excluding sales tax).

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly on a rolling 12-month basis.
- Split by channel (store, app, web) and by loyalty tier.
- Staff purchases and test accounts are excluded.

## Source tables
- `sales_orders`: order value, discounts, order date
- `returns`: refunded value per order
- `customers`: customer id, loyalty tier, staff and test flags

## Dashboards
- Customer 360 Dashboard
- Executive KPI Pack

## Caveats and exclusions
- A value above 100% means the cohort spent more than in the prior year, even after churn.
- Merged customer records keep the earliest customer id.
- Not comparable with figures before v1.4, which did not deduct returns.

## Change history
- v1.4 (2025-10-01): returns now deducted, aligned with KPI-001.
- v1.0 (2025-01-15): first certified version.

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Customer Analytics
Status: Certified
Version: 1.4
Effective date: 2025-10-01
Domain: Customer

Conversion Rate (KPI-005) | part 1
# Conversion Rate (KPI-005)

## Definition
Conversion Rate is the share of app and web sessions that end in at least one completed order. It covers digital channels only. Store conversion is measured separately by Store Footfall Conversion (KPI-009).

## Formula
Conversion Rate % = Qualifying sessions with a completed order / Total qualifying sessions x 100

A qualifying session has at least one page or screen view, lasts more than 5 seconds and is not flagged as a bot.

## Grain and filters
- Calculated daily.
- Split by platform (iOS, Android, web) and traffic source.
- Internal staff traffic is excluded.

## Source tables
- `app_sessions`: session id, platform, duration, bot flag
- `sales_orders`: order id, session id, status

## Dashboards
- Sales Performance Dashboard
- Digital Engagement Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- A session ends after 30 minutes without activity.
- Orders are linked to sessions by session id. If a customer browses on one device and buys on another, only the buying session converts.
- v2.0 figures are not comparable with v1.x because bot traffic was counted before.

## Change history
- v2.0 (2026-01-15): bot filter and 5-second rule added.
- v1.0 (2024-10-01): first certified version.

## Ownership and status

Status: Certified

wholesale partners and corporate gifting clients

Days Sales Outstanding (KPI-003) | part 1
# Days Sales Outstanding (KPI-003)

## Definition
Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) is the average number of days Kestrel takes to collect payment after invoicing a business customer. It only covers credit sales to wholesale partners and corporate gifting clients. Retail sales are paid at checkout and are out of scope.

## Formula
DSO = (Accounts receivable at period end / Credit sales in the period) x Number of days in the period

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly.
- Split by customer segment (wholesale, corporate gifting).
- Intercompany invoices are excluded.

## Source tables
- `invoices`: invoice amount, invoice date, due date, paid date, status

## Dashboards
- Executive KPI Pack

## Caveats and exclusions
- Disputed invoices stay in accounts receivable until they are resolved.
- Invoices written off as bad debt leave accounts receivable on the write-off date.
- A large invoice raised on the last day of a month can push DSO up for that month only.
- Standard payment terms are 30 days, so a DSO well above 30 means late payment.

## Change history
- v1.0 (2025-03-01): first certified version.

## Ownership and status
Owner: Head of Finance Analytics
Status: Certified
Version: 1.0
Effective date: 2025-03-01
Domain: Finance

# Marketing ROI (ROAS) (KPI-015)

## Definition
Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) is the net revenue generated by paid media for each unit of currency spent on it. It is the main marketing ROI measure at Kestrel.

## Formula
ROAS = Attributed net revenue / Paid media spend

Attributed net revenue is the Net Revenue (KPI-001) of app and web orders where the last paid click happened within 7 days before the order.

## Grain and filters
- Reported weekly and monthly.
- Split by channel and campaign.
- Only paid media spend is included; owned channels such as email are excluded.

## Source tables
- `marketing_spend`: campaign, channel, spend
- `sales_orders`: order id, net value, last paid click and click date

## Dashboards
- Marketing Effectiveness Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Provisional: the attribution method (last paid click versus a data-driven model) is still under review.
- Store sales influenced by online ads are not attributed, so ROAS understates total impact.
- Not approved for board reporting or the Executive KPI Pack.

## Change history
- v0.9 (2026-03-01): attribution window set to 7 days.
- v0.6 (2025-11-01): first draft.

# Active Customer (30-day) (KPI-006)

## Definition
An Active Customer is an identified customer (loyalty member or account holder) who completed at least one purchase in any channel (store, app or web) in the last 30 days. Anonymous buyers cannot be counted.

## Formula
Active Customers = Count of distinct customer ids with at least one completed order where the order date is between (run date - 29 days) and the run date

## Grain and filters
- Daily snapshot, reported weekly and monthly (month-end snapshot).
- Split by channel, region and loyalty tier.
- Staff and test accounts are excluded.

## Source tables
- `sales_orders`: customer id, order date, status
- `customers`: loyalty tier, staff and test flags

## Dashboards
- Customer 360 Dashboard
- Executive KPI Pack

## Caveats and exclusions
- Orders that are fully returned within the 30 days do not make a customer active.
- This KPI requires a purchase. It is not the same as Active User (KPI-020), which counts app logins without a purchase.
- The 30-day window is the only certified definition. Any other window (for example 90 days) is not certified.

## Change history
- v1.1 (2025-11-01): fully returned orders excluded.
- v1.0 (2025-02-01): first certified version, replacing informal team definitions.

# Dashboard Publishing Standard (SOP-06)

## Purpose
This standard sets the rules every dashboard must meet before it is shared outside its own team.

## Roles
- **Dashboard owner:** builds and maintains the dashboard; listed in the data catalog.
- **Data steward:** checks the dashboard against this standard before publishing.

## Rules
1. Every published dashboard must have an entry in the data catalog with an owner, a refresh schedule and its linked KPIs.

## Steps to publish
1. The dashboard owner requests a review in the data service portal.
2. The data steward checks rules 1 to 7 and records the result.
3. If all rules pass, the dashboard is published and its catalog entry is updated.

## Purpose
This procedure explains how a KPI moves from Provisional to Certified. Only Certified KPIs may be used in the Executive KPI Pack and in board packs.

# Data Quality Incidents (SOP-05)

## Purpose
This procedure explains what to do when a KPI or dashboard shows wrong or missing data.

## Roles
- **Reporter:** anyone who spots the problem.
- **Data steward:** triages the incident and sets the severity.
- **KPI owner:** communicates with users and signs off the fix.

## Severity levels
- **P1:** a Certified KPI in the Executive KPI Pack is wrong or missing.
- **P2:** any other Certified KPI or Certified dashboard is wrong or missing.
- **P3:** a Provisional KPI, a single report or a cosmetic issue.

## Steps
1. The reporter logs a "Data incident" in the data service portal with a screenshot and the KPI id.
2. The data steward sets the severity within 1 hour for P1 and within 1 working day for P2 and P3.
3. For P1 and P2, a warning banner is added to every affected dashboard within 2 hours.
4. The KPI owner tells key users what is affected and when a fix is expected.
5. The fix is tested and the banner is removed once the KPI owner signs off.
6. For P1 incidents, a root cause note is written within 5 working days and shared at the next KPI Council.

# Kestrel Retail Group: Data Governance Policy

POL-01 | Version 3.0 | Effective 2025-01-01 | Owner: Head of Data Governance

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets how Kestrel Retail Group defines, owns and certifies the data and KPIs used for decisions.

## 2. Scope

All KPIs, dashboards and source tables listed in the data catalog, in every channel (stores, app and web).

## 3. Roles

The KPI Council, chaired by the Head of Data Governance, approves certification and major changes. Each KPI and data asset has one accountable owner, a domain head named in the data catalog. Data stewards check definitions and data quality.

## 4. Certification levels

Certified: approved by the KPI Council and safe for board reporting. Provisional: in use but not yet approved; must be labelled on dashboards and must not be used in board packs. Deprecated: replaced by a newer version; must not be used for any reporting.

## 5. Principles

There is one certified definition per KPI. Informal definitions in team notes, slides or FAQs have no standing; when they conflict with a Certified KPI definition, the Certified definition applies.

## 6. Compliance

Breaches are reported to the Head of Data Governance. Procedures supporting this policy are SOP-01 to SOP-08.

# Customer Churn Rate (KPI-007)

## Definition
Customer Churn Rate is the share of recently active customers who stop buying from Kestrel. A customer has churned when 180 days pass without a completed purchase in any channel.

## Formula
Churn Rate % = Customers in the start base with no purchase for 180 days by quarter end / Customers in the start base x 100

The start base is every identified customer with at least one completed order in the 180 days before the quarter starts.

## Grain and filters
- Reported quarterly, with a monthly rolling view.
- Split by loyalty tier, region and first purchase channel.
- Staff and test accounts are excluded.

## Source tables
- `customers`: customer id, loyalty tier, account status
- `sales_orders`: customer id, order date, status

## Dashboards
- Customer 360 Dashboard
- Executive KPI Pack

## Caveats and exclusions
- A customer who closes their account counts as churned immediately.
- This v2 replaces v1 (KPI-007-V1), which counted account closures only. v1 is Deprecated and its figures must not be compared with v2.
- Churn is reported one quarter after the fact, because the 180-day window must pass first.

## Change history
- v2.0 (2026-04-01): 180-day inactivity definition approved by the KPI Council under SOP-03.
- v1.0 (2025-01-01): account-closure definition, now Deprecated.

# Data Retention (SOP-08)

## Purpose
This procedure sets how long Kestrel keeps data and documents, and how they are deleted.

## Roles
- **Data owner:** makes sure their tables follow the retention periods.
- **Platform team:** runs the monthly deletion jobs.
- **Head of Data Governance:** approves any exception.

## Retention periods
- `sales_orders`, `returns` and `invoices`: 7 years, for finance and tax audit.
- `customers`: while the account is open, then 2 years after closure.
- `app_sessions`: 25 months.
- `nps_responses`: 3 years.
- `marketing_spend`, `inventory_snapshots` and `deliveries`: 5 years.
- Deprecated KPI definitions: 2 years after deprecation, then archived.

## Steps
1. Deletion jobs run on the first Sunday of each month.
2. The platform team sends a deletion report to each data owner.
3. A customer request to delete personal data is completed within 30 days, unless finance law requires the order record to be kept. In that case the record is anonymised.

# Customer Acquisition Cost (KPI-014)

## Definition
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is the average marketing spend needed to win one new identified customer. A new customer is someone whose first ever completed order falls in the period.

## Formula
CAC = Acquisition marketing spend in the period / New customers acquired in the period

## Grain and filters
- Reported monthly and quarterly.
- Split by marketing channel (paid search, paid social, affiliates, print).
- Only campaigns tagged as acquisition are included.

## Source tables
- `marketing_spend`: campaign, channel, objective tag, spend, agency fees
- `customers`: customer id, first order date, acquisition channel

## Dashboards
- Marketing Effectiveness Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Brand and retention campaigns are excluded from spend.
- Agency fees are included in spend from v1.1.
- Channel-level CAC uses the acquisition channel recorded on the customer. Customers with no recorded channel only count in the total.
- Compare with Customer Lifetime Value (KPI-011) to judge payback, but note CLV is still Provisional.

## Change history
- v1.1 (2025-12-01): agency fees added to spend.
- v1.0 (2025-03-15): first certified version.

# Marketing ROI (ROAS) (KPI-015)

## Definition
Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) is the net revenue generated by paid media for each unit of currency spent on it. It is the main marketing ROI measure at Kestrel.

## Formula
ROAS = Attributed net revenue / Paid media spend

Attributed net revenue is the Net Revenue (KPI-001) of app and web orders where the last paid click happened within 7 days before the order.

## Grain and filters
- Reported weekly and monthly.
- Split by channel and campaign.
- Only paid media spend is included; owned channels such as email are excluded.

## Source tables
- `marketing_spend`: campaign, channel, spend
- `sales_orders`: order id, net value, last paid click and click date

## Dashboards
- Marketing Effectiveness Dashboard

## Caveats and exclusions
- Provisional: the attribution method (last paid click versus a data-driven model) is still under review.
- Store sales influenced by online ads are not attributed, so ROAS understates total impact.
- Not approved for board reporting or the Executive KPI Pack.

## Change history
- v0.9 (2026-03-01): attribution window set to 7 days.
- v0.6 (2025-11-01): first draft.
